resolved_conflicts.field: construction date of the earliest Duncan Peak structure
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not fully resolved. A 1941 newspaper gives 1913 for the old lookout. The register gives a 10-foot tower on the Little Bald Mountain site in 1910-1915, and a 1917 ground house just north of it. The information sheet says a tower was rebuilt in 1917 on the actual peak. The story reports each date with its source rather than choosing one.

resolved_conflicts.field: structure type of the 1917 building north of the current lookout
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls it a ground house and the information sheet calls it a tower. Both place it just north of the current lookout site, so the location is treated as agreed.

sources.title: Duncan Peak Lookout information sheet (Foresthill Ranger District, Tahoe National Forest)

notes_for_editor: The coordinates put this record about 1.2 km north-northwest of the Little Bald Mountain record (us-ca-duncan-peak-little-bald-mountain), which fits the register and information sheet saying the 1917 structure was just north of the current lookout. Early dates conflict (1913, 1910-1915, 1917). The 2009 Site of 1917 Cabin caption is the only site description and is not verified on the ground. The Forest Lookouts page also carries a 2013 American Fire note about a Duncan Peak lookout; it does not say which one, so it is left out. The Little Bald Mountain story already covers the 1910-1915 tower and the 1943 groundhouse.
